chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from one of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of sauces is vinegar; it breaks the bitterness, extinguishes the yellow bile, and revives the heart.'

key_terms.الصَّفْرَاءُ: Yellow bile (one of the four humors)
key_terms.الْإِدَامُ: A preserved food or sauce served with a meal

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of vinegar according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through the chain of Shaykh al-Kulayni, attributes to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) a saying of Imam Ali (AS) that elevates vinegar from a mere condiment to a holistic remedy within the framework of traditional humoral medicine. By describing it as breaking bitterness and reviving the heart, the text underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the integration of physical health (tibb) with spiritual vitality, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of valuing simple, natural foods for their restorative properties.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from one of our companions, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Samma, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘
The best of the sauces is the vinegar, it breaks the bitterness, and extinguishes the paleness, and revives the heart’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from certain persons of our people from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm from Shu’ayb from abu Basir who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘
The best sauce is vinegar, it breaks bitterness, (bile) extinguishes yellowness (gall) and brings the heart to life.’”
